sections.heading: 4. Run a document-backed pre-flight before accepting fixed rent
paragraphs: A production launch should mean one file can survive independent review from parcel identification through cash settlement. Build three lane-specific checklists rather than one generic real-estate form. The telecom lane needs the lease, estoppel where obtainable, rent history, assignment restrictions, lender position, and buyer pricing criteria. The billboard lane needs municipal sign authorization, state DOT permit status, transfer procedure, applicable spacing and lighting rules, and ground-lease continuity. 23 U.S.C. 131 establishes the federal highway advertising control framework; state implementation and local rules determine the particular site's operating constraints. A busy road and favorable AADT cannot substitute for a permit determination. The IOS lane needs written zoning confirmation for the proposed activity, lawful access, heavy-vehicle suitability, environmental review, drainage responsibilities, insurance, and a tenant demand test. Budget for specialist confirmation whenever an online map or informal telephone conversation cannot resolve a material issue. Save the authority's written response and identify its assumptions. If a variance or permit decision remains discretionary, make the commercial commitment contingent on the needed result rather than declaring the site ready because an application was accepted. Application intake and permission to operate are different milestones with different cash consequences.

Stress the cash calendar before testing a second geographic market. In the illustrative IOS example, one vacant month still requires $6,200 ground rent plus $800 site costs, a $7,000 cash drain before central overhead. That exceeds the entire $6,600 reserve of the smallest launch. At a $30,000 launch, the $16,500 reserve covers only about 2.36 months of those site obligations, again before central overhead. Therefore the reference yard is unsuitable for a thinly funded speculative master lease. Seek conditional commencement, a creditworthy committed subtenant, explicit owner-funded improvements, or a smaller obligation. Tenant security deposits are liabilities and may be restricted; do not silently spend them as ordinary revenue. For easement and billboard assignments, model a ninety-day closing delay with continuing legal expense and zero proceeds. For access assemblages, model failed survey findings and a buyer withdrawal separately. Count verbal investor interest as zero committed funding. A capital partner belongs in the forecast only after the relevant commitment and draw conditions are documented. Keep a signed decision record explaining which downside the reserve covers and which downside requires termination. Scaling means adding repeatable capacity, not spreading the same cash buffer across more correlated closing risks.

Launch with one accountable operator and three on-call specialists covering legal and title coordination, GIS and survey coordination, and environmental or site diligence as the active lane requires. Separate regulated professional work from administrative coordination; a contractor organizing survey files does not replace a licensed surveyor. The Scaled team adds a second full-time operator and a fourth contractor only when the file load and realized contribution support them. Track cash committed per surviving opportunity, days awaiting lender response, diligence dollars lost per terminated file, and retained contribution per completed closing. Review invoice exceptions weekly and cancellation deadlines daily. Before the first outward payment, test signer permissions, independent beneficiary verification, the accounting entry, and the document backup. Before the first yard opening, test emergency access, failed credentials, power interruption, and the tenant escalation contact. Before the first assignment closes, reconcile escrow instructions to the executed consideration and fee provisions. Record actual outcomes instead of treating scheduled work as completed. A launch file passes only when every material blocker has an owner, evidence of resolution, and a funded operating response. Preserve the ability to decline the next deal without endangering obligations already accepted on the current one.

callout.title: Four pre-flight checks before the first irreversible commitment
callout.body: A dated checklist is useful only when its attached evidence matches the transaction, the operating use, and the actual cash obligation.
items: Capital check: retain at least 50% of launch capital as working-capital reserve at initial allocation, then document downside coverage before each new commitment.
Rights check: confirm title, recorded access, assignment language, required lender SNDA, and any permit transfer conditions before exercising control.
Site check: complete the applicable environmental, stormwater, heavy-axle zoning, insurance, and emergency-access verification before IOS rent becomes unconditional.
Execution check: test bank beneficiary verification, signer authority, document recovery, and the gross-to-net accounting bridge before releasing closing funds.

chapters.pull_quote: Buy the evidence that protects your exit before buying the obligation that consumes your reserve.
action_checklist: Allocate startup capital using the exact budget matrix, place 55% in a separate reserve, and build a thirteen-week cash forecast excluding restricted funds.
Confirm current vendor checkout terms, provision the twelve-layer stack, and record every renewal, annual commitment, seat requirement, and payment-processing assumption.
Have local counsel review principal-versus-broker activity, entity authority, option contingencies, assignment rights, and required lender or permit consents.
Run one gis_landlocked_parcel_easement_assemblage file from GIS screening through recorded-rights review, survey scope, voluntary buyer economics, and a documented termination fallback.
Obtain site-specific insurance and environmental scopes before IOS commitments, then stress vacancy against rent, site costs, and central overhead.
Reconcile the three canonical scenarios to retained operator revenue, test payment and recovery controls, and complete the four pre-flight checks before launch.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #42, ranked Rank #11 of 42 with a 91/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, rewards document control rather than speculative property exposure. Across the volume's 11 mapped plays, the recurring killers are defective assignment rights, mortgage priority, nontransferable sign permits, uncovered yard obligations, and revenue recorded before collection becomes defensible. This chapter converts those defects into evidence requirements, exposure limits, and measurable stop conditions. Formula v2.0 preserves annual owner profit of $33,600 Conservative, $214,000 Base, and $494,000 Scaled; property principal and customer billings never inflate those cases. The adjacent solar equity play receives separate treatment because supported ownership allocations cannot become a freestanding depreciation product. Use the matrices to contain downside before deposits, guarantees, assignments, or investor representations become difficult to unwind.

sections.heading: 1. Buy enforceable rights, not persuasive parcel screenshots
paragraphs: The question's 80% figure is a framing device, not a measured failure rate. The observable failure pattern is buying one right while assuming it includes several others. A tower on an FCC Antenna Structure Registration record does not establish ownership of the rent, an assignable easement, carrier renewal intent, or access across neighboring land. Many structures do not require registration, so absence is not a universal rejection signal. Start with the recorded instrument, current title commitment, survey, lease amendments, payment ledger, and actual signatories. Reconcile parcel boundaries against access and utility corridors rather than accepting a broker's aerial markup. Separate the landowner's fee interest, the tenant's equipment interest, and the precise receivable being acquired. Check relocation clauses, termination rights, purchase options, rights of first refusal, and rent offsets before applying a multiple. A perpetual easement can outlive a cancellable revenue contract; perpetual land rights do not manufacture perpetual carrier payments. Treat any missing executed amendment as a pricing blocker, not an administrative item. Assign one contractor to abstract documents and another to verify exceptions against originals. The operator signs the exception register only after every economic assumption points to an identifiable document and clause.

The second trap is confusing a seller's signature with survival against the seller's lender. Obtain the mortgage, recording sequence, lender contact, and applicable consent requirements before committing nonrefundable capital. An SNDA must address the actual instrument and contemplated transfer; a generic tenant form may not protect purchased easement income. Foreclosure priority and enforceability depend on documents and state law, so title counsel must identify which interests survive and which require express lender recognition. Track consent age from delivery of a complete package, not from the first unanswered email. As an internal rule, escalate after fourteen calendar days without substantive response and stop additional discretionary diligence spending after thirty unless the seller extends exclusivity and deposit protection. These are spending controls, not statutory deadlines. Keep tenant estoppels separate from lender recognition: an estoppel can confirm payment facts without changing mortgage priority. Never represent a pending consent as received. If the lender demands a release payment, include it in the closing waterfall and rerun the spread. The fallback is a conditional option extension or a documented withdrawal, not an unsecured promise to obtain signatures after closing.

The third trap is treating 16×–22× tower pricing as an available exit rather than a negotiation range requiring buyer underwriting. Consider an illustrative $24,000 annual contractual rent stream acquired at 18× for $432,000 and resold at 20× for $480,000. The scorecard spread is $48,000, not $480,000; $12,000 of unreimbursed closing and diligence costs leaves $36,000 before other business expenses. If the buyer reduces the acceptable annual rent to $21,600 and holds the 20× multiple, proceeds fall to $432,000 and the entire spread disappears before costs. Measure rent eligibility separately from the headline multiple. Exclude unverified reimbursements, temporary incentives, and payments subject to unresolved offsets. Require the buyer's written underwriting conditions before assuming a simultaneous closing eliminates funding risk. With $12,000–$60,000 startup capital, a $432,000 acquisition cannot quietly become a balance-sheet purchase. Use a properly documented assignable option or independently funded closing structure only when the contracts support it. If the buyer withdraws, the fallback must be expiration with bounded loss, not a personal guarantee large enough to consume several years of modeled owner profit.

callout.title: Four document habits that protect the actual spread
callout.body: Experienced operators price exceptions before negotiating the headline multiple.
items: Send the proposed easement and assignment to the lender together; recognition of the old lease alone may leave the new interest exposed.
Obtain the buyer's definition of eligible annual rent before quoting a 16×–22× range to the landowner.
Maintain separate survey layers for leased area, access, utilities, and expansion rights; a single parcel outline conceals expensive gaps.
Negotiate exclusivity extensions tied to documented consent delays while keeping deposit-release conditions explicit and independently verifiable.

sections.heading: 2. Make billboard permits and IOS liabilities survive the downside case
paragraphs: Digital billboard beginners often secure a ground lease before learning that the desired sign cannot legally occupy the site. Section 131 of title 23 establishes the federal highway advertising framework, while state DOT rules, federal-state agreements, and local ordinances determine critical spacing, location, lighting, and permit requirements. A DOT AADT count measures traffic exposure, not entitlement. An existing static sign permit does not automatically authorize digital conversion, and a lawful nonconforming sign may lose protected status after relocation, reconstruction, or excessive interruption. Obtain written agency treatment of the exact parcel, sign dimensions, faces, technology, and contemplated transfer. Confirm whether the permit attaches to an owner, operator, structure, or location and what filing completes assignment. For an illustrative $30,000 assignment fee, a $6,000 application expense and $4,000 option payment consume one-third of gross fee economics before overhead. If denial leaves both amounts unrecoverable, underwriting the $30,000 as probable cash is reckless. Link option exercise and assignment payment to defined permit milestones. The fallback is abandoning the application within a capped budget, not installing hardware while a variance remains unresolved.

IOS operators make an analogous mistake when they equate vacant industrial land with a permitted heavy-fleet yard. Confirm the actual use classification, outdoor storage allowances, truck circulation, axle loading, operating hours, screening, lighting, fire access, and any restrictions on fueling or repair. The absence of a building does not remove drainage, pavement, security, or environmental costs. A Phase I environmental site assessment addresses historical and current environmental conditions within its scope; it does not certify stormwater capacity or grant operating permits. For acquisition structures relying on CERCLA landowner protections, counsel and the environmental professional must evaluate all appropriate inquiries and continuing obligations. Lessee protections require their own analysis. Ask whether the intended activity falls within industrial stormwater permitting and identify the applicable state program, discharge route, and responsible operator. Never assume that a landlord's old permit covers a different tenant's activities. Obtain contractor estimates for drainage and surfacing before lease execution. A $35,000 unexpected drainage repair exceeds the Conservative annual owner profit of $33,600. The circuit breaker is a termination right tied to documented diligence findings, with restoration and investigation responsibilities allocated before possession.

The NNN label is another trap: allocating costs in a contract does not ensure a tenant can pay them. Build the master lease and sublease into a single obligation calendar covering rent commencement, escalation, renewal, insurance, taxes, maintenance, surrender, and casualty. In an illustrative yard, customer billings of $18,000 monthly less $12,000 head rent produce a $6,000 retained spread, or $72,000 annually on the scorecard basis. Another $2,000 monthly of unrecovered maintenance and security reduces contribution to $48,000 before central overhead. Customer billings of $216,000 are not the modeled operator revenue. Three months without customer collections still require $36,000 head rent, before other costs, even if RFID access has been suspended. Track collected occupancy rather than occupied spaces alone. For this example, freeze expansion when cash receipts fall below head rent plus unavoidable site expenses for two consecutive months. Use deposits and enforceable credit support as contractual protection, without counting refundable deposits as earned spread. Review lawful notice and access procedures before restricting a defaulting customer's vehicles. A remote controller must never become an improvised repossession system.

callout.body: Each verification requires an identified reviewer, dated evidence, and a written exception decision.

sections.heading: 3. Detect clawbacks, accounting inflation, and access bans before cash disappears
paragraphs: Reconcile every deal to the same economic denominator before interpreting margin. Formula v2.0 uses annual scorecard revenue of $120,000, $535,000, and $950,000 with owner profit of $33,600, $214,000, and $494,000 respectively. The implied total cost envelopes are $86,400, $321,000, and $456,000. These are annual business cases, not promises that each individual transaction earns its case margin. Team assumptions remain 1 FT + 3 C for Conservative and Base, and 2 FT + 4 C for Scaled. The $2,000–$12,000 monthly operating range does not replace the complete annual expense reconciliation; deal costs, contractor costs, and other modeled expenses still need explicit treatment. Maintain a bridge from gross counterparty cash movements to net easement spreads, assignment fees, and retained IOS spreads. Institutional acquisition principal and tenant billings belong in separate columns. This management basis does not dictate financial-statement presentation: ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis applies where relevant, while lease accounting can fall under ASC 842. Have the accountant determine presentation from the contracts. Never force gross lease receipts into net accounting merely to match a scorecard, or count the same retained spread twice.

Clawbacks often arrive through documents that looked routine during closing: purchase-price true-ups, rent prorations, survival of representations, indemnities, escrow holdbacks, and obligations to cure title defects. Build a liability ledger with trigger, beneficiary, maximum contractual exposure, survival period, insurance response, and payment deadline. Treat uncapped environmental indemnities and personal guarantees as separate investment decisions rather than standard signature pages. For an illustrative $40,000 assignment fee with a $10,000 unresolved holdback, only $30,000 is immediately available cash; the remaining amount is not an additional fee when released. Recognition and collectibility require the accountant's contract analysis, while treasury still needs actual bank availability. Track held or disputed amounts divided by earned fees, days since closing, and expected claim severity. Escalate when held or disputed amounts exceed 10% of trailing twelve-month fees, an internal concentration limit rather than an industry benchmark. Separately alert when any claim can consume more than 25% of the applicable annual owner profit. For Base, that trigger is $53,500. A single $60,000 indemnity dispute therefore deserves owner attention even when annual revenue remains on target. Preserve closing evidence and stop distributions that would leave contractual obligations without funded coverage.

Data shortcuts create another asymmetric loss channel. FCC records, DOT traffic datasets, county GIS layers, commercial parcel services, and advertising marketplaces have different access conditions and update cycles. Public availability does not authorize bypassing authentication, defeating rate limits, reusing another customer's credentials, or redistributing licensed records. Forged ownership documents, fabricated agency correspondence, and misleading listings can cause account termination and contractual or statutory liability. Treat a permission denial as a stop signal, not an instruction to rotate identities. Track source license, retrieval date, parcel identifier, verification status, and allowed reuse for every lead. On an HTTP 429 response, honor documented retry instructions and pause the affected job; repeated access denials require provider clarification before restarting. These controls protect continuity without teaching evasion. Keep underwriting documents in an access-controlled repository and minimize personal information in exported lists. A suspended listing account should trigger an approved provider appeal and continuity through already authorized channels, never substitute accounts created to defeat the suspension. Before relying on automation, verify ten sampled records against authoritative documents; any material ownership or entitlement error holds the batch for correction. Pipeline volume cannot compensate for systematically misidentified rights or unauthorized data access.

sop_steps.action: Export commitments, unrestricted cash, held fees, guarantees, and open claims into one dated ledger.
sop_steps.detail: Separate bank availability from earned revenue and isolate customer deposits from operating liquidity.

sop_steps.action: Match each forecast payment to its executed contract, collectible amount, consent status, and bank evidence.
sop_steps.detail: Flag missing amendments, disputed rent, incomplete assignments, and nontransferable permits before refreshing forecasts.

sop_steps.title: Apply the downside circuit breakers
sop_steps.action: Recalculate vacancy coverage, eligible tower rent, permit-denial loss, and surviving contractual claims.
sop_steps.detail: Use the chapter's internal thresholds as initial policies, then document tighter deal-specific limits where exposure warrants.

sop_steps.action: Assign a reviewer, spending ceiling, deadline, and exit route to every material exception.
sop_steps.detail: Resume commitments only after the underlying evidence changes; a revised spreadsheet alone does not cure a defect.

sections.heading: 4. Quarantine solar allocation risk and make every fallback executable
paragraphs: The mapped play solar_tax_equity_depreciation_strip_syndication, Commercial Solar Tax-Equity Flip & Bonus-Depreciation Strip Syndication, belongs to TRACK_1 and requires a different control stack from land-rights arbitrage. Arrange commercial solar partnership-flip investments only around genuine equity ownership, supported tax allocations, and actual cash-flow rights. Depreciation is a deduction allocated under applicable tax rules, not a standalone transferable credit. Illustratively, if reviewed facts support a $20,000 depreciation allocation and the investor can currently use it at a 30% marginal rate, the arithmetic tax reduction is $6,000, not $20,000 of sale proceeds. Basis, at-risk, passive-activity, timing, and other limitations can reduce or defer that result. A $100,000 equipment invoice does not establish the current deduction without eligible basis, placed-in-service evidence, applicable recovery rules, and any required basis adjustments. Do not hard-code bonus depreciation percentages without confirming the governing acquisition and service dates. Section 704(b) allocation requirements and section 7701(o), when relevant, demand substantive analysis rather than marketing labels. Keep this adjacent play outside the tower multiple model: investor subscriptions and project equipment cost are neither easement spreads nor operator fee revenue.

A partnership flip is also not simply a promised date when the sponsor takes all remaining economics. Model capital accounts, distribution priorities, allocation changes, transfer restrictions, and the specific negotiated flip trigger. Separate investment tax credit exposure from depreciation consequences: section 50 can recapture investment credit following specified events, while asset dispositions can raise depreciation recapture and other tax issues under different rules. In a simplified illustration, an originally allowed $30,000 investment credit subject to an applicable 60% recapture percentage produces $18,000 of recapture before other effects. The applicable percentage depends on the actual event and timing; a contract cannot eliminate the government's claim by assigning the economic burden elsewhere. Review which party indemnifies whom, whether that party has resources, and whether distributions leave adequate reserves. Securities offering requirements and intermediary registration also require review before solicitation. Transaction-based compensation can create broker-dealer concerns; calling it consulting compensation does not resolve the underlying conduct. The prescribed fallback is to suspend solicitation and closing, use appropriately licensed intermediaries, and restructure only as independently reviewed genuine equity ownership. Neither a disclaimer nor a revised slide deck repairs unsupported tax economics.

Build the final control system around maximum cash at risk rather than the number of opportunities sourced. The volume's eleven-play coverage should not imply eleven interchangeable legal structures or eleven additive revenue lines. Here the operating checks span tower sourcing, rent verification, easement acquisition, lender recognition, buyer placement, billboard entitlement, permit assignment, IOS use diligence, yard lease matching, remote billing, and the separately identified solar equity play. Treat these as control workstreams, not invented canonical play identifiers. For each live transaction, write the cancellation deadline, sunk cost ceiling, surviving liability, cash funding source, and person authorized to stop work. An illustrative $60,000 starting balance less $15,000 reserved for existing obligations and $18,000 for three months of $6,000 operating expense leaves $27,000 for bounded new commitments, not $60,000. Expected resale proceeds do not replenish that capacity until available. Hold a weekly exception review and require original evidence for every status change. Measure success by closed exceptions, cash actually retained, and losses avoided through timely withdrawal. Walking away from an unbounded guarantee is a completed operating decision, not a failed acquisition.

chapters.pull_quote: The best spread is the one that survives the missing signature, the empty yard, and the buyer who walks.
action_checklist: Build a rights register linking every tower rent assumption to recorded instruments, executed amendments, tenant evidence, and mortgage-priority review.
Obtain site-specific DOT and municipal determinations for billboard technology and transfer mechanics before releasing nonrefundable option or equipment payments.

chapters.title: Sourcing, Demand Mining & Landing Your First Deals
chapters.subtitle: Mine FCC ASR, State DOT AADT, Recorder Instruments & FMCSA Triggers; Convert Verified Buyer Demand into Assignable Infrastructure Rights
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #42, ranked #11 of 42 with a 91/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, rewards operators who source enforceable rights against documented demand rather than collect property lists. This chapter maps 11 sourcing plays across telecom easements, digital billboard assignments, and Industrial Outdoor Storage fleet yards. Build parcel-level evidence, interview actual buyers, and secure conditional control before committing capital. Treat FMCSA authority and inspection signals as prompts for relevant research, not proof of parking demand or invented filing deadlines. The annual owner-profit cases are $33,600 Conservative, $214,000 Base, and $494,000 Scaled. A measured 2–6-month campaign targets the first 3-to-10 signed wins while separately tracking conditional agreements, completed transfers, collected fees, and occupied yards.

sections.heading: 1. Map eleven sourcing routes around verified exit demand
paragraphs: Start with the exit, not a countywide owner blast. Select one freight corridor and its adjoining telecom and outdoor-advertising markets, then interview five infrastructure buyers, three billboard operators, and ten fleet dispatchers. Ask each buyer for acquisition geography, minimum remaining term, assignment restrictions, tenant concentration limits, and required closing documents. Ask fleet operators for actual overnight tractor counts, trailer dwell, access hours, turning dimensions, and their current cost per usable space. Record requests as dated demand briefs, with a named decision maker and an expiry date for pricing assumptions. A dispatcher describing congestion is a research source; a fleet manager accepting a specified yard rate and move date is a qualified prospect. Keep these categories separate in Airtable or a spreadsheet. The eleven routes below are this chapter's mapped sourcing plays, not eleven independent businesses to launch simultaneously. Choose one primary rail and one adjacent rail sharing the same geography. The opening objective is three independently verified demand briefs before paying for extensive title work or site engineering. If buyers refuse to specify a buy box, continue interviews rather than manufacturing inventory from public records. That sequence protects the $12,000–$60,000 startup budget from attractive parcels with no practical exit.

For telecom, download available FCC Antenna Structure Registration records, preserve registration identifiers, and spatially join coordinates to county parcel boundaries using QGIS. ASR identifies registered structures; it does not enumerate every rooftop installation or establish who owns the income stream. Cross-check assessor ownership, recorder easements, building permits, and the landlord's actual lease. Prioritize fragmented ownership, recent estate transfers, and leases whose access or assignment language can be clarified without impairing the carrier's operations. For billboards, combine state DOT outdoor-advertising inventories, AADT counts, municipal sign codes, and surveyed road geometry. A high traffic count does not create a digital conversion entitlement: spacing, lighting, interchange restrictions, and local sign prohibitions can destroy the apparent spread. For IOS, start with industrial parcels near documented dispatch bottlenecks, then inspect legal truck access, usable paved or stabilized area, drainage, and neighboring uses. Satellite imagery is a screening layer, never evidence of lawful storage. Create one immutable parcel identifier and attach each source's retrieval date. Resolve boundary ambiguity before mailing an owner, especially where a tower, access road, or proposed sign straddles separate tax parcels. A wrong-party conversation wastes scarce outreach capacity and can produce a worthless option.

Underwrite the rights you can convey, not the landmark you can photograph. Suppose an assignable telecom income interest produces $24,000 annually: a 16× acquisition costs $384,000, while a buyer accepting 18× would pay $432,000. The $48,000 difference is a preliminary spread before transaction costs, not $432,000 of operator revenue. A 22× exit is only a sensitivity until a buyer prices the actual tenant, term, escalators, and remedies. With startup capital far below the purchase price, negotiate conditional assignment rights or arrange a documented simultaneous closing; never assume the seller will finance an unfunded purchase. An illustrative billboard assignment paying $35,000 against $15,000 of documented project acquisition and direct costs leaves $20,000 on the scorecard fee basis. An IOS yard collecting $11,000 monthly against $6,000 of underlying rent leaves $5,000 before operator overhead and any unrecovered site expenses. Confirm who bears taxes, insurance, repairs, and stormwater costs rather than treating NNN language as an expense eraser. If assignment fails, fall back to an expressly permitted option extension or release the site. If the only remaining activity is arranging another party's transaction, verify the applicable brokerage authority before pursuing a fee.

callout.title: Extract the difficult facts before buying expensive diligence
callout.body: Veteran operators win by locating the document or decision maker that can invalidate a promising site before the next dollar is committed.
items: Ask telecom buyers for three recent rejection reasons, then make those exact defects searchable CRM fields.
Request the billboard permit file and transfer procedure, not merely a photograph of the existing sign face.
Walk an IOS yard with the prospective tenant's longest vehicle and measure turning conflicts before quoting total capacity.
Ask the recorded lender which department handles non-disturbance agreements before negotiating a closing date with the owner.

sections.heading: 2. Turn public signals into qualified opportunities without inventing intent
paragraphs: Implement fmcsa_dot_inspection_trigger_arbitrage as a fleet-demand research workflow, not an assertion that every new carrier needs a yard. Schedule a daily job to check authorized FMCSA Census, Licensing & Insurance, and public SMS resources for new source versions; ingest only what each source actually publishes. Census extracts and SMS products have their own update schedules, and SMS measures are generally refreshed monthly. Do not describe a monthly snapshot as a live roadside violation feed or bypass restrictions on inspection details. Store USDOT number, relevant docket identifier, source date, authority status, operating geography, fleet size, and a reason for research. Deduplicate by USDOT number before resolving a business contact. Newly granted authority and recently applied-for authority are different events. The often-repeated mandatory 21-day insurance-filing window is not a universal federal deadline; verify application processing, protest timing, insurance filings, and activation requirements separately against the carrier's actual record. A fresh HOS or maintenance issue may justify asking about parking or inspection space, but neither proves that a yard solves the violation. Never imply that FMCSA selected your company, that your service activates authority, or that purchasing parking satisfies federal operating requirements.

Make the trigger economically testable. In an illustrative weekly batch, review 100 source changes, retain 30 carriers operating inside the selected corridor, identify 12 with a plausible parking constraint, and seek six held discovery calls. If research and outreach cost $600, acquisition expense is $100 per held call; if only three calls occur, it doubles. One resulting tenant taking 20 spaces at $175 monthly generates $3,500 of yard billings, not $3,500 of retained profit. Allocate underlying rent and incremental servicing costs before comparing that tenant with other demand sources. Use a transparent private compliance-agency identity only when that accurately describes the business, and otherwise identify the actual private yard operator. Offer a free BOC-3/MCS-150 status-check worksheet linking to official records, explaining that process-agent designation and registration updates are separate obligations. Collect contact details through a voluntary callback request rather than suggesting government affiliation. When public inspection detail is unavailable, use inbound hand-raisers, dispatch interviews, and carrier-requested location searches. Do not substitute scraped driver identities or sensitive incident narratives. Track both accepted and rejected hypotheses so that a weak trigger loses budget instead of becoming permanent campaign folklore.

Score every property against six evidence dimensions totaling 100 points: verified demand 25, legal control 20, use feasibility 20, economic spread 15, counterparty authority 10, and timing 10. An 80-point threshold earns paid diligence only if every fatal defect has been resolved or made an explicit, enforceable closing condition. A high aggregate cannot compensate for prohibited truck storage, a nontransferable sign permit, or a seller lacking authority. For IOS, confirm the specific use with the planning department, investigate environmental conditions through an appropriately scoped Phase I, and determine industrial stormwater exposure under the applicable permitting program. An environmental report does not itself authorize discharge or cure historic contamination. For telecom, reconcile the rent schedule with actual receipts and request lender subordination, non-disturbance, and attornment terms where necessary. For billboards, document state and municipal requirements independently under the Highway Beautification Act framework. Save the negative answer and its source alongside the attractive economics. Assign one owner to clear each exception, with a specific deadline and maximum expense. Freeze further spending when a dependency slips beyond the option period; negotiate an extension before ordering additional reports.

callout.body: Treat these checks as independent requirements. A strong buyer quote does not repair defective title, unlawful use, or inaccessible property.

sections.heading: 3. Run a measured contact cadence and answer objections with evidence
paragraphs: Separate owner outreach from buyer recruitment because their reasons to respond differ. An owner receives a specific observation about a verified asset and a proposed next conversation; a buyer receives a concise fit statement against an already documented acquisition brief. For a tower landlord, write that you purchase defined lease-income interests and would like to review remaining term, rent, and assignment provisions. For a billboard landowner, identify the parcel and explain that any proposal depends on permit transferability and local authorization. For a fleet, lead with location, measured spaces, operating hours, surface, and the proposed monthly rate, then ask whether those particulars solve an existing dispatch problem. Avoid invented urgency, guaranteed proceeds, and references to private circumstances inferred from public filings. Use business email, individually researched calls, postal letters, and permission-based introductions. Maintain suppression across every channel. Commercial email must satisfy 15 U.S.C. 7704, including accurate headers, required sender information, and a functioning opt-out. Telephone campaigns must account for 47 U.S.C. 227 and applicable state restrictions; a published number is not blanket permission for automated texts. Start manually so the operator can hear objections before automating a flawed message.

Use six purposeful touches over 21 days, stopping immediately after an opt-out and changing the next step when the recipient replies. The first message establishes parcel relevance; the second tests whether you reached the right person; the third supplies one useful observation or document request. Later touches offer a defined review slot, address the actual objection, and close the loop. Do not send six versions of an empty follow-up. If an owner says the price is too low, show the income, term, buyer multiple, direct costs, and retained spread assumptions; ask which input they dispute. If they refuse exclusive control, propose a short, clearly bounded conditional option only where that structure is lawful and useful. If a fleet says the yard is expensive, compare usable spaces and route miles rather than discounting an unmeasured parcel. If a lender delay blocks a tower transaction, request a dated consent workplan and adjust the option period instead of promising a faster closing. An objection is a request for evidence or a genuine rejection. Record the difference, and stop working a prospect whose stated requirements cannot fit the economics.

Publish inbound pages only for inventory characteristics you can substantiate: a corridor parking brief, an infrastructure income-rights document checklist, and a billboard feasibility intake form. A yard page should distinguish available inventory from locations being researched, with no fabricated availability. Ask for vehicle count, dimensions, arrival date, required access hours, and preferred contact method; avoid collecting driver credentials or unnecessary personal information. Send a useful response within one business day and route qualified requests to the same CRM stages as outbound prospects. Track source, message version, cohort date, contact outcome, qualified demand, site review, signed control, and collected proceeds. As an illustrative planning benchmark, 500 raw records might yield 150 desk-qualified prospects, 60 substantive conversations, 24 demand or acquisition briefs, 12 site packs, six signed conditional controls, and three completed monetizations. These are working targets, not observed market averages. The respective stage conversions are 30%, 40%, 40%, 50%, 50%, and 50%. Measure owner-side and buyer-side funnels separately before joining them at a matched site. Review results weekly by cohort; a large list cannot compensate for unresolved use restrictions or buyers who never accepted the price.

sections.heading: 4. Land the first wins without confusing signatures, principal, and profit
paragraphs: Sequence the first 2–6 months around dependencies rather than a promised closing date. During weeks one and two, choose the corridor, interview buyers, configure source records, and produce three usable demand briefs. During weeks three through six, research the first cohort, run manual outreach, and complete inexpensive document checks. During weeks seven through twelve, concentrate on the few sites with verified control, feasible use, and a buyer or tenant willing to review terms. Reserve months four through six for lender responses, permit transfers, environmental work, and negotiated closings where needed. Track a signed mandate, conditional option, completed assignment, and occupied master lease as separate events. Three-to-ten signed wins can include conditional agreements, but a dashboard must never present those as three-to-ten paid transactions. A mandate counts only when the operator is authorized to provide the contracted service. Attach the actual conditions, termination rights, expiry date, and cash exposure to every agreement. If the first batch produces conversations but no document access, repair trust and specificity; if document access produces no viable sites, repair screening. Increasing message volume is the wrong response to defective inventory or unsupported buyer pricing.

Reconcile production targets to Formula v2.0 without treating underlying asset consideration as sales. The Conservative case is $120,000 annual scorecard revenue at 28%, yielding $33,600 owner net profit; the Base case is $535,000 at 40.0%, yielding $214,000; the Scaled case is $950,000 at 52%, yielding $494,000. The implied annual operating cost envelopes are $86,400, $321,000, and $456,000 respectively on that same economic basis. The illustrative production bridges below reconcile exactly but are not additional canonical assumptions. Their IOS components assume twelve productive months, so a yard opened halfway through the year earns only half that annual spread unless another transaction offsets the difference. Startup capital of $12,000–$60,000 and monthly baseline opex of $2,000–$12,000 are separate planning ranges; they do not replace the scorecard's full annual expense envelope. Keep deposits and acquisition principal on a distinct cash schedule. The scorecard uses retained transaction economics, not gross tenant collections or institutional purchase prices. Actual statement presentation requires contract-specific analysis, including ASC 606 principal-versus-agent treatment where applicable and ASC 842 for lease arrangements. Apply no invented retained-share percentage to figures already supplied on a retained basis.

Keep the operating team smaller than the opportunity list. At Conservative and Base, the prescribed structure is one full-time operator plus three contractors; at Scaled, it is two full-time operators plus four contractors. Assign the founder demand interviews, negotiations, and capital decisions, while contractors handle source research, specialist document review, and site diligence within defined scopes. A contractor slot is capacity planning, not permission for an unqualified person to perform regulated work. Automate source-version checks, parcel joins, consent-document assembly, and reminders before automating outbound volume. Install RFID access and recurring NNN billing only after the yard's lawful use, tenant obligations, and emergency access are settled. Every Friday, reconcile signed agreements to the cash ledger and list the next irreversible commitment. Require actual demand evidence before increasing fixed rent exposure. If 30 targeted conversations produce no acceptable price, revisit the corridor or offer; if counterparties agree on price but closings stall, fix consent packaging and control periods. The first repeatable win is not a lucky signature. It is an identifiable signal, a verified right, a documented counterparty need, and collected spread that survives all required costs.

sections.heading: 1. Turn parcel signals into transferable, fundable rights
paragraphs: Start with a rights inventory, not a list of attractive parcels. Import FCC Antenna Structure Registration records, state DOT annual average daily traffic layers, county assessor rolls, and recorded parcel geometry into QGIS. ASR coverage is incomplete for the telecom universe, so supplement rooftop and smaller structure leads with recorded leases and owner-authorized documents. Every intake record needs a jurisdiction, parcel identifier, source snapshot date, owner contact provenance, and proposed transaction type. Separate tower easement acquisition, billboard permit-linked assignment, and IOS seasonal master leasing before scoring; each purchases different rights and fails for different reasons. The intake script uses integer cents and a deterministic source key, preventing a refreshed assessor export from creating another payable opportunity. Its score prioritizes documented spread and evidence completeness, not legal eligibility. Preserve the original export and its SHA-256 digest outside the database, then store that digest with subsequent verification events. A contractor may collect records, but only the designated deal lead can confirm ownership against title evidence. Missing instruments trigger a document request, while confirmed nonassignability ends that branch before deposits or engineering invoices accumulate against a speculative exit.

Underwrite tower rights from the actual rent schedule, escalation clause, remaining term, renewal rights, termination language, and access easement. An illustrative $30,000 annual eligible rent stream purchased at 16 times rent costs $480,000; a buyer paying 18 times rent offers $540,000. After $15,000 of transaction charges, the retained spread is $45,000, not $540,000. The advertised 16–22 times range is a screening reference, never an executable bid. Obtain buyer-specific pricing and settlement instructions before committing acquisition capital. With only $12,000–$60,000 startup capital, use a permitted assignment or an escrow-controlled, buyer-funded simultaneous closing rather than pretending the team can warehouse six-figure easements. Review existing mortgage priority and obtain the required lender subordination, nondisturbance, and attornment agreement, or an equivalent approved instrument appropriate to the transaction. A perpetual easement does not make the associated tenant rent perpetual. Model tenant termination and equipment removal separately. If lender execution outlasts the option period, negotiate a documented extension before expiry; otherwise release the transaction and preserve the buyer relationship. Do not silently replace a missing consent with a higher assumed exit multiple.

For billboards, connect traffic counts to a legally usable display location rather than converting AADT directly into advertising revenue. Check state-controlled route coverage, spacing, lighting, digital conversion rules, municipal zoning, and whether the permit and ground lease can transfer together. A $50,000 assignment receipt less $20,000 of directly attributable acquisition and closing charges creates a $30,000 retained assignment spread. For IOS, document heavy-axle use, turning geometry, drainage, access hours, fire access, and environmental conditions before accepting rent liability. One activated month with 100 occupied spaces at $600 produces $60,000 tenant billings; a $35,000 head-lease obligation leaves $25,000 retained spread before operating overhead. The cohort below assumes only four contracted activation months annually and no rent liability outside them. If the owner requires twelve paid months, rebuild the economics rather than retaining the seasonal case. NNN language allocates specified expenses; it does not erase the operator's contractual liability. Keep the scorecard's retained economic basis separate from statutory reporting: lease accounting generally belongs under ASC 842, while applicable service and assignment arrangements require their own ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment and recognition analysis.

callout.body: The best small-team advantage is early discovery of a document defect that would otherwise consume weeks of buyer attention.

Ask the billboard buyer to underwrite the permitted face and digital operating restrictions, not a traffic-count screenshot or an assumed future conversion.

sections.heading: 2. Implement six modules with serialized writes and explicit recovery
paragraphs: Use the following six modules as a local SQLite reference implementation, not as an unattended bank integration. Save each code cell under its indicated filename in one project directory. Initialize with sqlite3 from Python by executing schema.sql through Connection.executescript, then execute views.sql the same way. The remaining Python files expose callable functions; qa.py runs directly after initialization. Every writer enables foreign keys, waits for the database lock, and executes BEGIN IMMEDIATE before reading mutable business state. This serializes read-modify-write operations across processes sharing this local database. Unique source keys collapse repeated intake, event keys bind retries to their original payload, and a partial unique index prevents two settlement postings for one deal. A reused key carrying different content raises an error rather than overwriting evidence. If the process fails before commit, SQLite rolls back the transaction; after commit, the same key returns the recorded result. Keep the database on a supported local filesystem, not a shared network drive. Multiple hosts require a database such as Postgres with corresponding row locks, uniqueness constraints, and transaction boundaries, not synchronized copies of this SQLite file.

The state machine deliberately excludes remote side effects. It can qualify, verify, place into escrow, or scrub an opportunity, but it cannot wire funds, submit a permit, or create an easement. Verification events carry the digest of an evidence packet whose title, consent, zoning, and environmental conclusions were reviewed by the responsible specialists. A digest proves which packet was used; it does not prove that the conclusions are correct. CLOSED is reached only through a settlement posting that checks the current ESCROW state and records balanced cash and retained-revenue entries in the same database transaction. Consequently, competing settlement workers cannot both close and recognize the same deal. External settlement remains a separate process: use the escrow provider's transaction reference, retain its final statement, and confirm actual bank receipt before posting. A timeout while asking a provider for status means query that reference again, not issue another payment. When a provider supports idempotency keys, reuse the same stable key; otherwise use a documented single-operator release procedure. Local atomicity cannot manufacture exactly-once behavior inside an unrelated bank or government filing portal.

The ledger is intentionally narrow: it records cash-settled retained revenue, operating expense, and refundable deposits. Signed journal amounts use debit-positive convention. Settlement debits CASH and credits REVENUE; expense debits OPEX and credits CASH; deposit receipts credit DEPOSIT rather than revenue. Finalization requires at least two balanced lines, and triggers prevent edits to posted entries. The reconciliation view distinguishes operating profit from cash movement because deposit liabilities can move cash without creating earnings. Refunds reverse the deposit movement through a separately keyed posting. This is a transaction-control subledger, not a replacement for the statutory general ledger: accruals, lease assets, taxes, distributions, and correction entries need a separately specified accounting interface. For the illustrated cohort, earned spreads and expenses settle within their stated months, with no deposit balance or unpaid accrual at quarter end. Run QA after every import and before issuing the owner statement. Back up through SQLite's backup API, verify restoration, and preserve evidence files alongside their digest manifest. Database triggers constrain ordinary application writes; filesystem permissions and restricted deployment access must prevent unauthorized schema changes or direct replacement of the database.

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS deal (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    source_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    payload_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    play TEXT NOT NULL,
    spread_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(spread_cents >= 0),
    score INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
    state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NEW'
        CHECK(state IN ('NEW','QUALIFIED','VERIFIED','ESCROW','CLOSED','SCRUBBED')),
    version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS event (
    event_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    deal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES deal(id),
    payload_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    target TEXT NOT NULL,
    evidence_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS posting (
    posting_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    payload_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    deal_id INTEGER REFERENCES deal(id),
    kind TEXT NOT NULL
        CHECK(kind IN ('settlement','opex','deposit','refund')),
    month TEXT NOT NULL,
    evidence_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'DRAFT'
        CHECK(status IN ('DRAFT','POSTED')),
    CHECK(kind != 'settlement' OR deal_id IS NOT NULL)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS one_settlement_per_deal
ON posting(deal_id) WHERE kind = 'settlement';
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS journal (
    posting_key TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES posting(posting_key),
    line_no INTEGER NOT NULL,
    account TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(account IN ('CASH','REVENUE','OPEX','DEPOSIT')),
    cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(typeof(cents) = 'integer' AND cents != 0),
    UNIQUE(posting_key, line_no)
);
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS posting_insert_draft
BEFORE INSERT ON posting WHEN NEW.status != 'DRAFT'
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Insert draft before balanced finalization'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS posting_finalize
BEFORE UPDATE OF status ON posting WHEN NEW.status = 'POSTED'
BEGIN
    SELECT CASE WHEN
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM journal WHERE posting_key = OLD.posting_key) < 2
        OR
        (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cents), 0) FROM journal
         WHERE posting_key = OLD.posting_key) != 0
    THEN RAISE(ABORT, 'Posting requires balanced journal lines') END;
END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS posting_no_edit
BEFORE UPDATE ON posting WHEN OLD.status = 'POSTED'
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Posted records are immutable'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS posting_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON posting WHEN OLD.status = 'POSTED'
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Posted records are immutable'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_insert_draft
BEFORE INSERT ON journal
WHEN COALESCE((SELECT status FROM posting
              WHERE posting_key = NEW.posting_key), '') != 'DRAFT'
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Journal insertion requires draft posting'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_no_edit
BEFORE UPDATE ON journal
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Replace draft lines instead of updating'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS journal_no_delete_posted
BEFORE DELETE ON journal
WHEN (SELECT status FROM posting
      WHERE posting_key = OLD.posting_key) = 'POSTED'
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'Posted journal lines are immutable'); END;
Initialize before workers start; uniqueness and immutable posting triggers constrain every writer

from __future__ import annotations
import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3

ALLOWED = {
    "NEW": {"QUALIFIED", "SCRUBBED"},
    "QUALIFIED": {"VERIFIED", "SCRUBBED"},
    "VERIFIED": {"ESCROW", "SCRUBBED"},
    "ESCROW": {"SCRUBBED"},
}

def advance(event_key, deal_id, target, evidence_hash, db="ledger.db"):
    if not event_key or len(evidence_hash) != 64:
        raise ValueError("Event key and SHA-256 evidence digest are required")
    int(evidence_hash, 16)
    payload = [deal_id, target, evidence_hash]
    digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload).encode()).hexdigest()
    con = sqlite3.connect(db, timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
    try:
        con.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
        con.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        old = con.execute(
            "SELECT payload_hash FROM event WHERE event_key = ?", (event_key,)
        ).fetchone()
        if old:
            if old[0] != digest:
                raise ValueError("Event key content conflict")
            con.commit()
            return target
        row = con.execute(
            "SELECT state, version FROM deal WHERE id = ?", (deal_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None or target not in ALLOWED.get(row[0], set()):
            raise ValueError("Disallowed state transition")
        changed = con.execute(
            "UPDATE deal SET state=?, version=version+1 WHERE id=? AND version=?",
            (target, deal_id, row[1]),
        ).rowcount
        if changed != 1:
            raise RuntimeError("Concurrent state change")
        con.execute(
            "INSERT INTO event(event_key,deal_id,payload_hash,target,evidence_hash) "
            "VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)",
            (event_key, deal_id, digest, target, evidence_hash),
        )
        con.commit()
        return target
    except Exception:
        if con.in_transaction:
            con.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        con.close()
Evidence review happens before invocation; serialized transition checks prevent competing state changes
posting.py posts balanced cash events and closes settled deals atomically

from __future__ import annotations
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3

PAIRS = {
    "settlement": ("CASH", "REVENUE"),
    "opex": ("OPEX", "CASH"),
    "deposit": ("CASH", "DEPOSIT"),
    "refund": ("DEPOSIT", "CASH"),
}

def post(key, kind, month, cents, evidence_hash, deal_id=None, db="ledger.db"):
    if not key or kind not in PAIRS or type(cents) is not int or cents <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Posting requires key, supported kind, and positive cents")
    parsed = datetime.datetime.strptime(month, "%Y-%m")
    if parsed.strftime("%Y-%m") != month:
        raise ValueError("Month must use four-digit year and two-digit month")
    if len(evidence_hash) != 64:
        raise ValueError("SHA-256 evidence digest is required")
    int(evidence_hash, 16)
    payload = [kind, month, cents, evidence_hash, deal_id]
    digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload).encode()).hexdigest()
    con = sqlite3.connect(db, timeout=30, isolation_level=None)
    try:
        con.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
        con.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        old = con.execute(
            "SELECT payload_hash,status FROM posting WHERE posting_key=?", (key,)
        ).fetchone()
        if old:
            if old != (digest, "POSTED"):
                raise ValueError("Posting key conflict or incomplete posting")
            con.commit()
            return key
        if kind == "settlement":
            row = con.execute(
                "SELECT state FROM deal WHERE id=?", (deal_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            if row != ("ESCROW",):
                raise ValueError("Settlement requires escrow state")
        con.execute(
            "INSERT INTO posting(posting_key,payload_hash,deal_id,kind,month,"
            "evidence_hash) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)",
            (key, digest, deal_id, kind, month, evidence_hash),
        )
        debit, credit = PAIRS[kind]
        con.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO journal(posting_key,line_no,account,cents) VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
            [(key, 1, debit, cents), (key, 2, credit, -cents)],
        )
        con.execute("UPDATE posting SET status='POSTED' WHERE posting_key=?", (key,))
        if kind == "settlement":
            con.execute(
                "UPDATE deal SET state='CLOSED',version=version+1 WHERE id=?",
                (deal_id,),
            )
        con.commit()
        return key
    except Exception:
        if con.in_transaction:
            con.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        con.close()
Unique settlement index plus one transaction prevents duplicate recognition even under different retry keys
views.sql reconciles recognized retained revenue, expenses, deposits, and monthly cash

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS monthly_reconciliation AS
SELECT
    p.month,
    -SUM(CASE WHEN j.account='REVENUE' THEN j.cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS revenue_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN j.account='OPEX' THEN j.cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS opex_cents,
    -SUM(CASE WHEN j.account IN ('REVENUE','OPEX')
              THEN j.cents ELSE 0 END) AS profit_cents,
    SUM(CASE WHEN j.account='CASH' THEN j.cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS cash_delta_cents,
    -SUM(CASE WHEN j.account='DEPOSIT' THEN j.cents ELSE 0 END)
        AS deposit_delta_cents
FROM posting AS p
JOIN journal AS j ON j.posting_key=p.posting_key
WHERE p.status='POSTED'
GROUP BY p.month;
Compare bank movement with cash delta; profit differs whenever refundable deposit balances change

sections.heading: 3. Make specialist review, tax appeals, and exception ownership explicit
paragraphs: Assign the Base team as one full-time principal and three contractor functions: title and transaction counsel, environmental and civil diligence, and GIS plus bookkeeping operations. Contractor functions describe responsibility, not a promise that one person holds every professional credential. The principal owns pricing, buyer commitments, cash exposure, and the weekly exception meeting. Counsel resolves assignment restrictions, brokerage status, recorded interests, and closing instruments. The environmental professional controls Phase I scope and findings; the civil specialist confirms drainage and access where needed. Operations maintains source snapshots, deadlines, posting evidence, and reconciliation. Separate the person preparing a payment instruction from the person independently confirming escrow destination details through an established contact channel. Buying or assigning a principal interest does not automatically satisfy every state licensing exemption; document the exact local rule and the actual conduct performed. When activity is brokerage, engage the required licensee rather than renaming a commission. Contractor invoices must reference the deal and work product so that failed diligence remains visible in acquisition cost. Review aging weekly by the specific missing instrument and responsible counterparty, not by a vague probability-of-closing percentage.

The mapped play property_tax_assessment_appeal_contingency adds a separate, deadline-driven service queue rather than magically increasing tower rent. Ingest county valuation rolls when annual notices release, normalize parcel class and valuation date, and compare assessed-to-market ratios across genuinely comparable neighbors. An AVM flag starts review; it is not proof of unequal assessment or a permitted filing position. For illustration, a supportable $200,000 reduction multiplied by a 2.0% applicable effective tax rate implies $4,000 annual tax savings. A 40% first-year contingency yields $1,600 service revenue only after the contract's verification and collection conditions are satisfied. Across ten successful parcels, that becomes $16,000 before specialist fees and filing costs. The operating range is 30–50% of the first year's verified reduction, not a percentage of property value or a recurring claim on future savings. Track the jurisdiction's actual deadline, service authorization, appeal basis, submission receipt, and final tax outcome. In regulated states, partner with licensed local property-tax consultants or attorneys of record and automate pre-deadline batch electronic filing through authorized channels. Keep this adjacent service outside the Base cohort dollars unless the annual model explicitly replaces another revenue component.

Treat statutory requirements as operating inputs with named evidence owners. The Highway Beautification Act, 23 U.S.C. 131, and 23 CFR Part 750 establish the federal outdoor advertising framework, while state programs and municipal rules determine the site's concrete restrictions. Federal eligibility is not a local sign permit. For IOS acquisitions where all appropriate inquiries matters, 40 CFR Part 312 governs that inquiry framework; an environmental professional must determine scope, timing, and any need for further investigation. A Phase I report neither authorizes stormwater discharges nor resolves every operational environmental obligation. Evaluate 40 CFR 122.26 and the applicable state program against actual industrial activity and exposure, rather than assuming every yard requires the same permit. Texas property-tax representation illustrates why the adjacent appeal service needs jurisdictional routing: Occupations Code Chapter 1152 addresses property-tax consultants, and Tax Code 41.44 addresses protest timing. Archive the applicable rule version and transaction facts with each decision. When facts change, such as a new vehicle class, revised digital display operation, or different appeal representative, reopen the corresponding review before continuing work under stale evidence.

sections.heading: 4. Walk three monthly cohorts from source records to reconciled owner cash
paragraphs: The Worked 90-Day Cohort Walk is a constructed production case, not a report of completed transactions. Begin with $60,000 operator cash and no receivables, deposits, borrowings, or existing lease obligations. Month 1 sources cohort A's 60 opportunities. Forty-eight fail desktop screening; of 12 reviewed candidates, nine fail document or economic diligence and three advance. No retained revenue arrives that month, while $18,000 of paid operating costs creates an $18,000 cumulative operating deficit and leaves $42,000 cash. In Month 2, two cohort A tower assignments settle for retained spreads of $20,000 and $25,000. Their underlying easement purchase principal moves through buyer-controlled escrow and never enters this operator cash schedule. Month 2 also sources cohort B's 60 opportunities: 50 fail desktop review and eight of ten diligence candidates are scrubbed, leaving a billboard assignment and an IOS activation. Paid Month 2 costs total $27,000, so $45,000 receipts generate $18,000 operating cash and restore the opening $60,000 balance. Scrubbed leads create no fictional revenue write-off; their consumed labor and diligence invoices remain inside the operating cost schedule.

Month 3 receives $30,000 from cohort A's billboard assignment, $33,750 from cohort B's billboard assignment, and $25,000 retained IOS spread from cohort B's first contracted activation. Those five completed transactions produce quarterly retained revenue of $133,750. Month 3 sources cohort C's 60 opportunities; 52 fail desktop screening, six more fail diligence, and two remain documented carry-forward candidates with no recognized revenue. Month 3 paid operating costs are $35,250, leaving $53,500 incremental cash and $113,500 closing cash. The cost schedule separates recurring overhead of $4,000, $5,000, and $6,000 from variable professional, acquisition, diligence, and closing support costs of $14,000, $22,000, and $29,250. These variable costs are additional to charges already deducted in computing retained deal spreads; never post the same charge twice. Thus recurring monthly overhead stays within the stated $2,000–$12,000 range while total production costs can exceed it. To reproduce the ledger, post settlements of 2000000, 2500000, 3000000, 3375000, and 2500000 cents against five separately verified ESCROW deals, and post monthly expense totals of 1800000, 2700000, and 3525000 cents.

Quarterly profit equals $133,750 minus $80,250, or $53,500, giving exactly 40.0% margin. Four equivalent production blocks yield $535,000 annual retained revenue, $321,000 costs, and $214,000 owner net profit. The annual construction contains eight tower assignments totaling $180,000, eight billboard assignments totaling $255,000, and four IOS activation months totaling $100,000 retained spread. It does not assume twelve IOS rent months or add repeat revenue from the same activation. Cohort C remains pipeline, not an extra cash asset. Repeating production requires replenishing buyer capacity, maintaining the same cost discipline, and signing seasonal terms that actually support four paid activation months. A delayed $33,750 billboard closing shifts cash and recognition into the later period; it cannot remain in Month 3 merely to preserve the target. The separate Conservative case remains $120,000 revenue less $86,400 costs, producing $33,600 at 28%; Scaled remains $950,000 less $456,000, producing $494,000 at 52%. Base and Conservative use one full-time operator plus three contractors; Scaled uses two plus four. These are distinct annual assumptions, not automatic outcomes of multiplying the lead count or shortening specialist review.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #42 ranks #11 of 42 with a 91/100 Money-to-Manpower Score because infrastructure lease spreads reward evidence quality more than headcount. This directory connects 11 mapped plays to FCC registrations, recorded instruments, DOT traffic and sign records, municipal enforcement events, environmental layers, and controlled yard telemetry. The desk converts those sources into verified rights, priced exceptions, and executable assignments rather than speculative property lists. Formula v2.0 annual owner profits remain $33,600 Conservative, $214,000 Base, and $494,000 Scaled. Sixteen named resource entries distinguish access methods, purchasing tiers, refresh uncertainty, request discipline, and fallback evidence. sections.heading: 1. Build the rights-and-events spine before buying enrichment
paragraphs: Organize the desk around eleven mapped operating plays, each requiring a different evidence packet: tower easement acquisition, rooftop telecom rights acquisition, easement resale, billboard ground-lease control, billboard permit assignment, digital-sign conversion screening, IOS master-lease acquisition, fleet-yard subleasing, lender SNDA resolution, unmanned yard access and billing, and municipal_code_violation_trigger_arbitrage. These are operating workstreams, not eleven additive revenue forecasts. Give every opportunity a durable internal identifier linked to county, parcel identifier, physical address, geometry, asset type, and instrument references. An FCC Antenna Structure Registration number identifies a registered structure; it does not identify every antenna tenancy, establish land ownership, or prove an assignable lease. Many rooftop installations will have no ASR record because registration requirements do not cover every structure. Start with ASR for applicable structures, then join assessor parcels and recorder instruments, retaining separate confidence scores for spatial proximity and legal identity. A tower point inside a parcel is a research lead, not proof that the parcel owner controls the relevant easement. Store original source coordinates and the transformed project coordinates so an analyst can reproduce a disputed match. Reject automated joins across adjacent parcels until a survey, recorded exhibit, or reliable site document resolves the boundary.

Acquire public records through documented bulk downloads, published APIs, or the portal's permitted export function. For FCC ASR, preserve the registration number, status, coordinates, structure height, registrant, and source retrieval date; retain the download documentation alongside the file. Use ULS separately when a relevant radio authorization needs corroboration, recognizing that spectrum authorization and property control answer different questions. County assessor systems contribute tax ownership and parcel geometry, while recorder systems supply deeds, mortgages, easements, assignments, releases, and recorded notices. Search the recorder by both parcel-linked names and instrument references because indexing practices vary and parcel search may omit older documents. A recently formed special-purpose entity can hold title while an operating company occupies the site. Do not substitute a commercial contact record for that distinction. Build an evidence chain from current vesting deed to controlling lease or easement, then to each amendment and assignment. For billboard prospects, add state DOT outdoor-advertising records and the local sign file before pricing an assignment. For IOS, request the actual zoning district, permitted-use text, site approvals, and conditions governing truck storage, surfacing, operating hours, and access. Record the issuing office whenever a portal omits an attachment.

Implement municipal_code_violation_trigger_arbitrage as an event service, not an indiscriminate address scrape. Poll municipal building portals and county recorder dockets daily where supported for failed structural or fire inspections, expired permits, code citations, and newly filed mechanic's liens. Normalize event type, event date, publication date, case number, parcel, responsible office, and current disposition. A lien filing is an allegation requiring document review; it is neither a judgment nor proof that the owner needs a specific contractor. Deduplicate by jurisdiction and case or instrument number, then suppress resolved, withdrawn, duplicate, or mislocated events. Route exclusive, timestamped remediation opportunities to an authorized contractor territory and send attorney-relevant records only under a permitted arrangement that avoids paid legal recommendations or fee sharing. Illustratively, 120 monthly events multiplied by 50% verified relevance and 25% contractor acceptance produce 15 accepted leads; at $80 each, contractor lead revenue is $1,200 before collection costs and $300 of review expense, leaving $900 before other overhead. That separate service example does not increase this volume's canonical forecast. If daily access is unavailable, use low-frequency scheduled API or bulk exports, disclose record age, and identify every outreach message as private commercial contractor or remediation assistance, never municipal enforcement.

callout.body: Spend research effort on contradictions between sources; those contradictions reveal both mispriced opportunities and deals that should be rejected.

sections.heading: 2. Enrich only after jurisdiction, geometry, and permitted use reconcile
paragraphs: Run enrichment as a waterfall with explicit stop conditions. First establish the parcel and jurisdiction from official geometry; second establish current vesting and recorded burdens; third establish the asset's permit and use status; fourth purchase missing ownership normalization or contact research. Commercial parcel coverage from Regrid or property records from ATTOM can accelerate joins, but neither should silently overwrite a conflicting official instrument. Save provider identifiers, source fields, retrieval timestamps, and match confidence independently. For an illustrative 200-parcel batch, a free jurisdiction screen rejecting 120 parcels leaves 80 for ownership review; a second screen rejecting 50 leaves 30 for licensed enrichment. At an assumed $2 per enriched record, purchased data costs $60 instead of $400. Those are budgeting assumptions, not vendor prices. Include analyst time: thirty files at twelve minutes each require six hours even when API retrieval takes seconds. Use a weekly exception queue to resolve ambiguous ownership, missing amendments, and parcel splits rather than repeatedly repurchasing the same records. For contact verification, prefer a counterparty's published business channel or a documented introduction. Do not infer permission for automated calling from the mere presence of a telephone number in a licensed dataset. Preserve opt-outs and channel restrictions with the contact record.

Use GIS to establish questions that a site visit and specialist review must answer. In QGIS, load parcels, ASR points, roadway centerlines, AADT stations, sign locations, zoning polygons, FEMA flood hazards, wetlands indicators, and known environmental facilities into a common projected coordinate system. Document units before buffering; a distance expressed in degrees is not a defensible spacing measurement. For billboards, state rules may measure spacing along a roadway or distinguish direction, interchange proximity, and controlled routes, so a simple circular buffer is only an initial filter. AADT counts vehicles, not verified advertising impressions, and the count station may represent a segment with different visibility or turning movements. For IOS, inspect flood exposure, drainage paths, nearby sensitive uses, access geometry, pavement condition, and recorded access rights. FEMA mapping does not describe every drainage problem, the Wetlands Mapper does not determine jurisdiction, and an empty EPA ECHO result does not establish clean property. Escalate potentially viable yards to an environmental professional and an appropriate Phase I scope before executing the master lease. Preserve the layer vintage, the actual source feature, and a screenshot of the analytical view so another reviewer can distinguish source facts from the analyst's interpretation.

Treat access reliability as an operating specification. The directory's refresh intervals are desk targets, not promises about government publication latency; every connector must record both source effective date and retrieval time. For ArcGIS REST FeatureServer services, inspect layer metadata for supported query formats, pagination, object identifiers, spatial reference, and maximum record count before choosing a batch strategy. Where supported, request identifiers first and fetch bounded groups with only necessary fields. Validate returned counts against the expected identifier set because a successful HTTP response can still contain a truncated result. Use conditional requests when a service supports them, honor Retry-After, back off after throttling, and stop when access terms prohibit automation. A portal login, CAPTCHA, or blocked response is a reason to request an export, not rotate identities. Budget for records requests, certified copies, and commercial coverage gaps instead of assuming every useful field has an API. Keep acquired personal information out of general-purpose screenshots and restrict contact exports to the people handling outreach. When a vendor contract restricts redistribution, send the contractor a permitted event summary rather than the underlying licensed dataset. Review official provider documentation at implementation time because endpoints, authentication methods, geographic coverage, and commercial entitlements change.
